newsitem.title: USA: IBM to unveil a digital broadcast package.
newsitem.headline: IBM to unveil a digital broadcast package.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. will announce Monday a digital broadcast package that will enable consumers to receieve many benefits of digital television without having to buy a digital TV.

The package, called Logicast, can be used by broadcasters and other companies until the industry makes its transition to digital television, which was approved by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission last week.
IBM will unveil Logicast Monday at the National Association of Broadcasters convention in Las Vegas.
While digital television was just approved, it will be at least 18 months before it comes into U.S. homes.

Digital TV offers crisp, clear pictures, CD-quality sound and it enables the transmission of up to 10 compressed digital programmes on the same cable bandwidth taken up by one analogue programme. Service providers will be able to offer more channels and new revenue-generating services, such as near video-on-demand and impulse pay-per-view and real-time news.

IBM said that until digital TV is available, LogiCast can be developed by broadcasters and others to offer some of these services, such as news, pre-selected Internet content, interactive education and enhanced advertising.

"From the consumer's viewpoint, there is a box next to their TV and they would use it to receive these services," said John Gardner, manager of market development for IBM's video enabled solutions. "You don't have to buy a new TV. For broadcasters, it gives them a starting point, a system they can use to make the transition (to high definition digital television)."

IBM said that the LogiCast package consists of a video server, which houses video; storage and networking products, key products and services from leaders in the broadcast industry; and IBM's project management and content services.

IBM will market LogiCast to broacasters, satellite service providers, cable and telephone companies to help them create new services as they build on the existing infrastructure to move gradually into digital broadcasting.

Some of the companies IBM is already working with include STET (Societa Finanziaria per Azioni), the Italian telecommunications giant, which now has an end-to-end digital broadcast solution installed and Hughes Electronics Corp.
IBM also plans to announce some partnerships at NAB with companies whose products and services will be used as part of the LogiCast package.
